subject: Renewal + Volume step-ups / blended rates — Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from today's renewal discovery call

Hi Maya / Tom — great to meet you both today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have the same assumptions before I put a formal pricing proposal on paper.

Key notes from discovery:
- Current usage: ~30M tokens/month across ingestion + chat routes.
- Expected ramp: customer engineering expects ~2–3x growth in Q3 and up to ~120M tokens/month by month 12 with a major new product route (customer search + summaries).
- Budget target (high-level): Maya indicated a target blended unit economics goal around $400–$600 per 1M tokens (across routes), pending quality checks.
- Priority routes: chat/generation (high latency SLO), embeddings for semantic search, and a new high-throughput summarization route.
- Procurement timeline: procurement team indicated aim to finalize terms within 4–6 weeks to hit April budget cycle.

What I'll send next (today):
1) Two pricing options (renewal with step-up volume tiers + blended-rate scenario) as an attachment so you can model costs at different ramp profiles.
2) Short note on how we handle adding new routes/models mid-contract (we support add-on routes and blended billing for multi-route usage).
3) A suggested mutual action plan with dates for contract review, security questionnaire handoff, and pilot/staging cutoff.

Attachments included with this thread: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (detailed tier math) and redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (one-pager).
[Attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (application/pdf)]

Action items for you: please confirm the following so I can finalize numbers:
- Confirm the 30M starting baseline and expected 12-month target (approx. 120M) — or provide a different ramp profile.
- Confirm target $/1M tokens range (you mentioned $400–$600 on the call).
- Confirm procurement point of contact and timeline to route the MSA + SOW.

Happy to jump on a short follow-up with procurement + engineering if that helps — I can book 30 minutes this week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Thanks Marissa — quick confirmations / clarifications:
- Baseline is correct: ~30M tokens/month today.
- Ramp: target is ~80–120M tokens/month within 12 months depending on staging success; assume a conservative plan of ~80M for budgeting but we can model to 120M.
- Budget: procurement is aiming for blended economics between $450–$600 per 1M tokens; preference toward the lower end but we'll need to run a quality eval first.
- New routes: yes — embeddings and a high-throughput summarization route. We need to understand if those count as separate routes for pricing or are included in blended consumption.
- Procurement POC: Tom Rivera (cc'ed) — procurement will need MSA + pricing SOW and will run standard security questionnaire.

Can you include an example monthly cost at 30M / 80M / 120M so we can see unit economics and total spend? Also call out any one-time onboarding or pilot credits.

— Maya
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap + next steps from today's renewal discovery call — pricing options attached

Thanks Maya — attaching the two-option pricing pack (see attachments):
- Option A: Standard renewal + step-up tiers
  • Tiers (example): 0–50M @ $700 / 1M tokens; 50–150M @ $525 / 1M; 150M+ @ $400 / 1M
  • This keeps list unit prices visible and automatically drops unit price as you hit higher tiers.
- Option B: Blended renewal (single blended $/1M across routes)
  • Example blended scenarios in attachment: 30M = $680/1M (total spend ~$20.4k); 80M = $560/1M (total spend ~$44.8k); 120M = $510/1M (total spend ~$61.2k) — these are illustrative blended outputs based on your projected route mix.
- Add-ons / new routes: We support adding routes mid-contract as an add-on SKU. By default new route usage is billed at the same tier pricing, and for customers who want a single blended invoice we can apply a rolling blended calculation monthly (as shown in the workbook).
- Promotional pilot: We can offer a 3-month promotional blended discount (applied to first 3 months of renewed term) to accelerate adoption — example numbers included.
- One-time items: onboarding (SLA enablement + integration support) typically billed as a one-time services fee; many customers opt to convert to credits instead (examples in the attachment).

Attachment callouts: pricing_model_v2.xlsx contains the tier math (sheet: volume-scenarios) and a "blended-example" sheet where I plugged your 30/80/120 numbers to produce the $/1M outputs. redwood_pricing_summary.pdf has the bullets for procurement.
[Attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx]
[Attachment: redwood_pricing_summary.pdf]

Next steps I propose:
- You (Tom/procurement) review the one-pager + ask any questions about MSA terms. I can drop a redlined MSA into DocuSign once we align on the pricing structure.
- Neha (cc) from Customer Success will schedule a technical onboarding + quality eval window with your team — suggested 2-week pilot.
- If you confirm the conservative ramp (80M) I'll send a draft SOW with the tiered and blended examples incorporated for procurement review.

Could we book a 30-minute call Thursday or Friday to walk procurement through the one-pager? I'm flexible; please share a time that works.

Best,
Marissa

Looping in quickly — Marissa, thanks for the clear options. Approve offering a 3-month promotional blended discount (commercial) to help Acme move to pilot. Two quick asks before we finalize:
1) Finance needs the exact wording for the promotional term and an example amortization across the first quarter. Can you add that to the SOW?
2) Product/Platform: confirm that adding the summarization route and embeddings will not require a separate commercial negotiation — we should treat as an add-on that inherits tiered pricing unless they ask for a dedicated SLA.

Neha — can you take point on scheduling the technical eval and capture any quality gating we should include in the SOW?

Rishi
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
